t: You're on East Smithfield, a short street in Tower Hamlets, and a small locality too. The name once covered more ground, the part of the ancient parish of St Botolph without Aldgate that lay outside the City of London. The poet Edmund Spenser was born here. He wrote The Faerie Queene, an epic poem celebrating the Tudor dynasty and Elizabeth the First, and he's considered one of the great poets in the English language. The Australian surgeon and soldier Robert Fowler was also born here.
